meta.title: Transmission-line reflections, standing waves and VSWR
meta.tools: 1-D FDTD solution of the telegrapher's equations (NumPy), bounce-diagram prediction
meta.summary: Launch a step and a sine onto a 50 Ω line terminated in 150 Ω, 50 Ω, open and short loads; compare the time-domain voltage at the source with the bounce-diagram prediction and the standing-wave ratio with (1+|Γ|)/(1−|Γ|).
meta.problem: What really happens when a fast edge hits a mismatched load, and how does that become a standing wave for a continuous sine?
meta.method:
Lossless line, L′ = 250 nH/m, C′ = 100 pF/m (Z₀ = 50 Ω, v = 2×10⁸ m/s), 1 m long, 400 cells, leapfrog update at Courant number 0.5, resistive source 25 Ω and resistive/open/short loads implemented as boundary conditions. Step
response vs bounce diagram; 1 GHz sine for VSWR.

rows.quantity: 150 Ω: voltage after first reflection returns (t = 2T+)
